nodes.statement: test_disconnect_default disconnects a running write-back cache using the default userspace flags.
Before disconnect, the test creates dirty data in a running write-back cache and records core CRCs.
The userspace disconnect API enters with flush_data enabled by default.
The userspace request crosses KCAS_IOCTL_DISCONNECT_CACHE into cache_mngt_disconnect_cache.
The kernel disconnect path acquires a cache reference for the target cache instance.
The disconnect path owns the cache reference while blocking new dirty data and stopping the cache.
With default flush_data true, the disconnect path flushes dirty cache data before stopping it.
The kernel path freezes exported object queues, locks the cache, and stops the running cache.
Failures while preventing dirty data or flushing branch to the disconnect error cleanup paths.
Error cleanup restores cache state and unwinds references according to the failure label reached.
Successful disconnect deposits and releases the acquired cache management references.
After reconnect, the test observes frozen exported queues, zero dirty blocks, and unchanged core CRCs.
test_disconnect_default is the functional oracle for default flush and post-reconnect data preservation.

edges.statement: The default disconnect is triggered only after the test has made the running WB cache dirty.
The dirty running cache and captured CRCs are passed into the default disconnect API flow.
The userspace API maps its default pass-through and flush flags into the disconnect ioctl.
The ioctl handler invokes cache_mngt_disconnect_cache, which obtains the target cache reference.
The acquired cache reference remains owned by the disconnect operation through state transitions.
While owning the cache, the default path prevents new dirty data and performs the requested flush.
Completing the dirty-data flush permits queue freeze, cache lock, and cache stop.
Any failure in the state-changing sequence propagates to a labeled disconnect cleanup path.
The error labels restore or unwind the partially changed cache state.
Both success and error cleanup release the cache references held by disconnect.
After disconnect resources are released and the cache reconnects, the test reads dirty count and CRC observations.
The functional test asserts zero dirty blocks and unchanged CRCs after the default disconnect lifecycle.

disconfirming_checks.statement: The explicit no-flush variant retains dirty data, demonstrating that the default zero-dirty result depends on flush_data true.
